title: Touch affordance audit: compact toggle, toast overlap, and embedded-chart momentum scroll
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Cross-browser responsive QA ticket focused on three recurring touch/scroll regressions seen across compact density surfaces. Goal is to triage, propose fixes, and land design tokens/interaction updates that prevent regressions on Safari iOS and Firefox Android without regressing desktop behavior.

Scope: compact toggle/button touch hit targets, toast/snackbar z-index and collision with floating controls, and momentum scrolling inside embedded charts/virtualized tables (swipe gap when list uses virtualization). Components affected: Toggle (compact), Button (compact), Toast/Snackbar, Chart canvas wrapper, Virtualized Table row container.

Steps to reproduce (examples seen in customer QA and internal e2e):
1) Compact toggle in dense toolbar (iPhone 14 Safari, zoom default): many toggles report missed taps -> touch target smaller than 44px in some density token combinations.
2) While a toast/success message is visible at bottom-right, opening a floating control (compact filter chip dropdown) causes visual overlap and prevents interaction with dropdown options (occurs in Firefox Android and Safari iOS).
3) Embedded line chart with pan/zoom in a scroll container on Android Firefox: momentum scroll cancels chart pan and leaves a 8-12px swipe gap between successive virtualized table rows when table is scrolled quickly (visual gap that persists until repaint).

Acceptance criteria:
- All compact toggles and compact buttons meet a >=44px touch target without changing visual density (using hit-area padding tokens).
- Toasts use a platform-aware stacking policy and an ingress/egress animation that doesn't steal pointer events from floating controls; dropdowns should appear above toasts when necessary and be clickable.
- Momentum scrolling/pan interactions for embedded charts do not break virtualization rendering and do not produce persistent swipe gaps on Firefox Android.
- Documented token changes (hit-area padding, z-index layers, scroll-snap and repaint hints) and integration tests added to e2e harness.

Design notes and proposed changes:
- Introduce token: token.touch.hitPadding.compact = 6px (adds invisible padding around compact controls).
- Define stacking token group: token.zindex.overlay.toast = 900, token.zindex.overlay.floating = 950; add platform override for iOS if required.
- For virtualized lists, add a repaint hint on fast scroll end (css will-change: contents + small delay) and add a 1px buffer to virtualization window to pre-render adjacent rows.

Files/links: Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/UI-Kit-Compact-Affordance (commented). Confluence spec draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UIKIT/Touch+Affordance+Audit. QA dashboard: https://datadog.redwood.ai/dashboards/qa-touch-affordance. Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/2345 (initial hit-area token patch).
updates: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after pairing with Support on two customer reproductions (Tenant A & Tenant B). Attached initial screen recordings and notes from remote session.

2026-02-28 - Priya Nambiar: Did a walk-through on Safari iOS 15 and found that visual density tokens collapse hit area in CSS; proposed adding padding via ::after pseudo element to avoid layout shifts.

2026-03-02 - Eng: ENG-14212 assigned to investigate virtualization window bug; early hypothesis: virtualization buffer too small when scroll deceleration triggers repaint throttling in Firefox Android.

2026-03-04 - Design review: Consensus to add token.touch.hitPadding.compact and to export example CSS snippet for engineering. Decided against increasing visual size of controls to preserve compact mode.
2026-03-06 - QA: Automated e2e added for compact toggle hit area on iOS simulator. Two intermittent flakes remain on BrowserStack (ticketed separately).

2026-03-08 - Eng: Draft PR created that implements hitPadding tokens and z-index layer for toasts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/2345. Engineering requests design approval on animation timing for toast ingress/egress.

2026-03-10 - Priya Nambiar: Reviewed PR, advised increasing toast entrance duration to 220ms and adding pointer-events: none to the transient backdrop; marked ready for dev review. Updated acceptance criteria with e2e checks.
qa_checks: manual: reproduce on Safari iOS (real device) and Firefox Android (real device)
automated: jest-dom+puppeteer touch target assertion >=44px for compact toggles
performance: e2e list virtualization smoke to assert no persistent gaps after 250 fast scroll cycles
notes: Trade-offs: increasing hit area via invisible padding preserves layout but may change hit-testing order for adjacent controls in very dense toolbars; we add an edge-case rule to fall back to a two-column collapse for extreme density toolbars. Will monitor metrics after rollout.
next_steps: Eng to land PR and coordinate with infra for canary rollout to hosted self-serve region us-east-1
Design to finalize tokens and publish migration guide for components that rely on legacy touch paddings
QA to run full suite across BrowserStack devices and prioritize any flakes into a follow-up patch
